topics.topic: Registry gateway behavior when per-call runtime-settings validation fails
questions: If this repeated full-environment validation fails during a Registry call, what failure crosses the gateway boundary?
What must a Registry operation answer when this new per-call full-environment validation fails, especially because an unrelated required setting became missing or invalid after startup?

If a per-Registry-call `load_runtime_settings` invocation fails after startup, especially because an unrelated required environment value became missing or invalid, what typed failure must `registry_gateway` return and may it make the HTTP request?

quotes: _registry_url: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST join only the supplied relative path to the Registry deployment URL, which is the registry_base_url field of the RuntimeSettings that the imported load_runtime_settings returns when this function calls it, and MUST preserve that URL's own path prefix so a Registry deployed under a prefix keeps it on every request; it MUST NOT read the process environment itself. A missing or empty URL never reaches this function, because load_runtime_settings refuses the service start for it, and this function MUST NOT catch, translate or repair a refusal of load_runtime_settings. Each of the following MUST raise RegistryBoundaryError carrying the transport_error member of = models.RegistryFailureKind, never a raw ValueError or other untyped error, and never a repaired URL: the URL is not a usable http or https base URL; it carries userinfo credentials, which are rejected rather than stripped, retained, or forwarded; the supplied path is absolute or protocol-relative, which MUST NOT be allowed to replace the host or scheme.
judgement.why: State 7 requires a per-call load_runtime_settings refusal to propagate without translation or repair, so no Registry HTTP request follows that refusal.

topics.topic: Whether Registry runtime settings are loaded once at startup or reloaded for every call
questions: Is `load_runtime_settings` executed once at process start, or executed again for every Registry call?
Must Registry calls use the RuntimeSettings snapshot loaded once at startup, as `runtime_settings` and A30 say, or reload the process environment for every call as this passage says?

Must `RuntimeSettings` be loaded once at startup and handed to `registry_gateway`, as `runtime_settings` and A30 say, or must the gateway call `load_runtime_settings` and reread the environment for every Registry call?

quotes:
A30's environment part: load, normalize, default and validate the closed
table `config.runtime_environment_variables` into `RuntimeSettings` once at
start, including the startup consistency of the binary bounds (A14). Factory
`38626cc7be12`.

`registry_gateway`
  takes the Registry URL from the `registry_base_url` field of the
  `RuntimeSettings` that `load_runtime_settings` returns, which it calls at
  each Registry call: the call reads and validates the environment again
  through `runtime_settings`, the same environment the start validated, and
  no settings object is handed to the gateway or cached by it (A6, A30; owner 2026-11-09: the Registry URL is read only through
  `runtime_settings`, SPEC_STANDARD 6.11).
judgement.why: One passage fixes environment loading once at startup while the other requires another complete load for every Registry call.

- a value that depends on the deployment (URLs, origins, hosts, size bounds,
  rate limits) — a row of the start-up table `config.runtime_environment_variables`,

  `RuntimeSettings`; the one exception is the two binary storage rows
  (`BINARY_STORAGE_ROOT`, `BINARY_MAX_READ_BYTES`), which have no field and

bases.rests_on:
The Registry URL is read only through `runtime_settings` (owner decision
2026-11-09, SPEC_STANDARD 6.11: a second reader of the environment is a
defect). `REGISTRY_BASE_URL` is a required variable of the start-up table that
R0-10's check covers, read into the `registry_base_url` field of
`RuntimeSettings`: a missing or empty value stops the start, and the Registry
gateway takes the value from the settings `load_runtime_settings` returns,
never from the environment.

precedent.topic: Where REGISTRY_ACTIVE_SEGMENT is owned and exported and how registry_gateway obtains it
quotes:
One Registry request to the active-project path `projects/active`, the
data-provider constants `REGISTRY_PROJECTS_PATH` and
`REGISTRY_ACTIVE_SEGMENT` joined (owner 2026-11-08, Q12), with no query
parameters, under the Registry timeout (`REGISTRY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`).

list_active_projects: [PROVENANCE] MUST resolve the Registry endpoint through _registry_url, apply a request timeout of the imported REGISTRY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS constant in seconds, and request exactly the path made of the imported REGISTRY_PROJECTS_PATH constant and the imported REGISTRY_ACTIVE_SEGMENT constant, joined by single slashes, relative to that endpoint with no query parameters; decoding still keeps only active ProjectReference values.
precedent.why: The later API and notes identify REGISTRY_ACTIVE_SEGMENT as a data-provider constant imported by registry_gateway and joined with REGISTRY_PROJECTS_PATH.

topics.topic: Which module loads and distributes validated runtime settings at startup
questions: Which module owns the startup call to `load_runtime_settings` and supplies the validated settings to the modules that need them?

quotes:
`module:runtime`, `module:staff_bootstrap_cli`, and `module:registry_gateway`
for the Registry URL (owner 2026-11-09, A30).

`module:runtime_settings` owns reading the environment, once: the closed table
`config.runtime_environment_variables`, defaults, normalization and the
startup checks (A30), into `RuntimeSettings`. `module:runtime` owns the
running application: one `PortalStore`, the inner application of `module:api`
mounted with the transport guard of `module:transport_guard`, and the two
health answers. `module:portal_store` owns the database connection and
creates every repository schema when a transaction begins. Crossing models:
`RuntimeSettings` from settings to runtime and guard; `HealthStatus` out.
judgement.why: The later API names runtime as a caller of load_runtime_settings, while the startup flow assigns environment reading to runtime_settings and application composition and settings distribution to runtime.
